data_notice: Public-sourced claim taken from an already-published URL. Probability is omitted where the original source did not state one word for word; those rows are verdict-only and are not in the Brier set. Link fields marked [U] are unknown and were not invented; those rows are reading-list items and are not scored.
exact_quote: Despite some predictions that AI will double US GDP growth, Acemoglu expects it to increase GDP by 1.1% to 1.6% over the next 10 years, with a roughly 0.05% annual gain in productivity.
question: Will AI increase US GDP by 1.1% to 1.6% over the 10 years from 25 Feb 2025, as Acemoglu expected on that date?
denominator: US real GDP at the start of the 10-year window (25 Feb 2025), with the increment attributed to AI
threshold: AI's contribution to US real GDP of 1.1% to 1.6% cumulative over 10 years (and a roughly 0.05% annual productivity gain, as context)
metric_unit: percent of US real GDP (cumulative AI contribution over 10 years)
resolution_rule: Numeric range. The 10-year window runs 25 Feb 2025 to 25 Feb 2035. KEPT if a published official or peer-reviewed estimate of AI's contribution to US real GDP over that window (Acemoglu-style task/TFP decomposition, or a CBO / BEA / equivalent attribution) falls in [1.1, 1.6] percent inclusive. The frozen target_value 1.35 is the midpoint; the pass band is the stated range itself (tolerance 0.25 around the midpoint). BROKEN if such an estimate exists and lies clearly outside [1.1, 1.6]. UNRESOLVABLE if, at the deadline, only total GDP is observed and no comparable decomposition isolating AI's contribution has been published — total GDP growth is not a substitute, because the claim is about AI's increment, not all growth. The exact_quote is Technology Review's 25 Feb 2025 wording of his expectation (not a first-person utterance in the interview); the numbers are the claim as stated on that public page that day. His 2024 paper used related but not identical figures (GDP +0.93–1.16%, TFP no more than 0.66%). This row resolves against the 25 Feb 2025 1.1–1.6% wording. A close miss outside the range is BROKEN.
resolution_source: Peer-reviewed or official decompositions of AI's contribution to US real GDP / TFP (CBO, BEA, or academic follow-ups in Acemoglu's framework) covering 2025–2035. BEA real GDP alone is not sufficient.
probability_note: No numerical probability was stated word for word by the original source; the claim is not in the Brier set.
basis: MIT Technology Review, 25 Feb 2025, stating Acemoglu's expectation of a 1.1–1.6% GDP increase over the next 10 years. No numerical probability was stated.
base_rate_or_reference_class: His 2024 paper 'The Simple Macroeconomics of AI' (task-exposure and task-level savings leading to modest TFP/GDP effects), contrasted on the same page with predictions that AI will double US GDP growth.
key_assumptions: The 10-year window is the decade after 25 Feb 2025.
A comparable published decomposition of AI's GDP contribution will exist at the deadline.
The 1.1–1.6% range on the 25 Feb 2025 page is the resolving range, not the paper's 0.93–1.16%.
update_triggers: A CBO, BEA, or major academic AI-attribution estimate.
A public retraction or restatement by Acemoglu.
